description.value: The Summit Lodge is a 9,000 square-foot facility perched at the summit of the Sea to Sky Gondola above Squamish, featuring a West Coast-inspired restaurant and café with local food and beverage options beneath dramatic floor-to-ceiling windows and Douglas fir beams. The lodge includes the Sky Pilot Restaurant, Co-Pilot Café, a viewing deck, and access to the Sky Pilot Suspension Bridge. Cyclists on the Sea to Sky corridor can reach it as a destination excursion from the gondola base station off Highway 99.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms Summit Lodge is a 9,000 sq ft facility at the top of the Sea to Sky Gondola, housing a West Coast-inspired restaurant and café, with washrooms explicitly listed under 'Summit Lodge Amenities Include.' No bike parking, water bottle refill, Wi-Fi, or other cycling-specific amenities are mentioned anywhere in the website content. The critical structural concern is that this venue is accessible only by gondola — touring cyclists must leave their bikes at the base and purchase gondola tickets to reach it, which fundamentally limits its role as a direct cycling stop.
concerns: Venue is accessible only via paid gondola ride — bikes cannot be ridden to the Summit Lodge; this is not a standard cycling stop.
No address in OSM record; venue sits at the gondola summit, not a street-addressable location.
No phone number in OSM record or on the fetched website pages.
Some listed amenities (Guest Services, Children's Play Area) are noted as seasonal.
The Basecamp facility at the gondola base may be a more relevant WWC listing for road-accessible cycling traffic.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The Summit Lodge is accessible exclusively by gondola — cyclists cannot ride to it directly and must leave their bikes at the base station and purchase gondola tickets. It may appeal as a destination excursion for Sea to Sky touring cyclists, but its suitability for the WWC directory depends on whether gondola-accessed venues are within scope; the base station (Basecamp) would be a more conventional WWC candidate.
enrichment_extras.notes: The gondola Basecamp at the base station (directly off Highway 99) may be a stronger WWC candidate for touring cyclists and could warrant a separate OSM record review.
